\[
L(f) = \ln\left(1 + \left|\mathcal{F}\{(I - \bar{I})\, w\}(f)\right|\right),\quad L(p) - \operatorname{median}_{|f| \approx |p|} L(f) \ge 3,\quad H = \prod_k \left(1 - e^{-D_k^2 / 2 D_0^2}\right)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(L\): The log magnitude of the windowed spectrum
- \(w\): A 2D Hann window
- \(p\): A peak frequency
- \(D_k\): The distance from notch center k in cycles per pixel
- \(D_0\): The notch radius

This is PixelNexus's own rule. The peaks are found in the spectrum of the image itself, with its mean removed and a 2D Hann window w applied. There, a periodic pattern makes a sharp peak. A peak is a local maximum of L in its 5 x 5 window. It must rise above the median of L on its ring, the frequencies at the same distance from the center, by at least the threshold. Only peaks at least the lowest frequency away from the center count. Each peak then gets a Gaussian notch, at its mirror points too, as in the notch-reject filter, and the image extended with the border mode is filtered.
